topic.name: Triple Integrals Over Type II Regions

question.text: Given that $R$ is the type II region shown above, $ \displaystyle \iiint\limits_R \sin{z} \: \textrm{d}V = $
question.explanation:
For a type II region $R$ with projection $D$ onto the $yz$-plane, the triple integral of a continuous function $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ is given by

\[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \,\textrm{d}V = \iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{u_1(y,z)}^{u_2(y,z)} f(x,y,z) \,\textrm{d}x \right] \textrm{d}A. \]

We consider the region $R$ as a type II region enclosed between the back surface $x = u_1(y,z) = 1$ and the front surface $x = u_2(y,z) = 2.$

So, the region $R$ is given by

\[ R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (y,z) \in D, \: 1 \le x \le 2 \right\}. \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type I plane region in the $yz$-plane with the upper curve

\[ z = 1-y^2. \]

Hence, $D = \left\{ (y,z) \: : \: 0 \le y \le 1, \: 0 \le z \le {1-y^2} \right\}.$

Therefore, we write the triple integral as follows:

\begin{align*} \iiint\limits_R \sin{z} \,\textrm{d}V &= \iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{1}^{2} \sin{z} \,\textrm{d}x \right] \textrm{d}A \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{1-y^2} \left[ \int_{1}^{2} \sin{z} \,\textrm{d}x \right] \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{1-y^2} \sin{z} \big[ x \big]_{x=1}^{x=2} \,\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{1-y^2} \sin{z} \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \end{align*}

example.title: Evaluating a Triple Integral Over a Type II Region Given a Diagram

question.text: Evaluate the mixed integral \[ \displaystyle \iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{0}^{\sqrt{y^2+z^2}} 4x \,\textrm{d}x \right] \textrm{d}A \] where the region $D$ in the $yz$-plane is given by \[ D = \big\{ (y,z) \, : \, 0 \leq y \leq 3, \: 0 \leq z \leq y \big\}. \]
question.explanation:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:

\begin{align*} \iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{0}^{\sqrt{y^2+z^2}} 4x \,\textrm{d}x \right] \textrm{d}A &= \iint\limits_D 2 \big[ x^2 \big]_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{y^2+z^2}} \,\textrm{d}A \\[5pt] &= \iint\limits_D 2\left(\left(\sqrt{y^2+z^2}\right)^2 -0\right) \,\textrm{d}A \\[5pt] &= \iint\limits_D 2y^2+ 2z^2\,\textrm{d}A \end{align*}

Next, we evaluate the double integral:

\begin{align*} \iint\limits_D 2y^2+ 2z^2 \,\textrm{d}A &=\int_{0}^{3} \int_{0}^{y} 2y^2+ 2z^2\: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{3} \left[ 2y^2z + \dfrac{2}{3} z^3 \right]_{z=0}^{z=y} \, \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{3} 2y^3 + \dfrac{2}{3}y^3 \, \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{3} \dfrac{8}{3}y^3 \, \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &=\left[ \dfrac{2}{3}y^4 \right]_{y=0}^{y=3} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2}{3}(81 - 0)\\[5pt] &= 54 \end{align*}

question.text: Evaluate the mixed integral \[ \displaystyle \iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{0}^{\sqrt{2z}} \dfrac{x}{2} \,\textrm{d}x \right] \textrm{d}A \] where the region $D$ in the $yz$-plane is given by \[ D = \big\{ (y,z) \, : \, 1 \leq y \leq 3, \: y \leq z \leq y+1 \big\}. \]
question.explanation:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:

\begin{align*} \iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{0}^{\sqrt{2z}} \dfrac{x}{2} \,\textrm{d}x \right] \textrm{d}A &= \iint\limits_D \dfrac{1}{4} \big[ x^2 \big]_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{2z}} \,\textrm{d}A \\[5pt] &= \iint\limits_D \dfrac{1}{4}(2z-0) \,\textrm{d}A \\[5pt] &= \iint\limits_D \dfrac{1}{2}z \,\textrm{d}A \end{align*}

Next, we evaluate the double integral:

\begin{align*} \iint\limits_D \dfrac{1}{2}z \,\textrm{d}A &=\int_{1}^{3} \int_{y}^{y+1} \dfrac{1}{2}z\: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{1}^{3} \dfrac{1}{4} \big[ z^2 \big]_{z=y}^{z=y+1} \, \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{1}^{3} \dfrac{1}{4}\left((y+1)^2 - y^2\right) \, \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{1}^{3} \dfrac{1}{4}(2y+1) \, \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{4} \left[ y^2+y \right]_{y=1}^{y=3} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{4}(9 +3) - \dfrac{1}{4}(1+1) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{5}{2} \end{align*}

question.text:
Evaluate the triple integral

\[ \displaystyle \iiint\limits_R y \: \mathrm{d}V \]

where the region $R$ is given by \[ R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (y,z) \in D, \: 0 \leq x \leq y+z+2 \right\}, \] and $D$ is a finite region in $yz$-plane enclosed between the $y$-axis, the $z$-axis and the line $z = 2-y$ in the first quadrant.
question.explanation:
Writing down our triple integral as a mixed integral, we obtain \[ \displaystyle \iiint \limits_{R} y \, \textrm{d}V = \iint\limits_{D} \left[ \int_{0}^{y+z+2} y \, \mathrm{d}x \right] \mathrm{d}A. \]

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants: \begin{align*} \iint\limits_{D} \left[ \int_{0}^{y+z+2} y \, \mathrm{d}x \right] \mathrm{d}A &= \iint\limits_{D} y \Big[ x \Big]_{x=0}^{x=y+z+2} \, \mathrm{d}A \\[5pt] &= \iint\limits_{D} y(y+z+2) \: \mathrm{d}A\\[5pt] &= \iint\limits_{D} y^2 + yz + 2y \: \mathrm{d}A \end{align*}

We must now evaluate the double integral above over the region $D$ in the $yz$-plane shown below.

We can evaluate our double integral as follows: \begin{align*} \iint\limits_{D} y^2 + yz + 2y \: \mathrm{d}A &= \int_{0}^{2} \int_{0}^{2-y} y^2 + yz + 2y \, \mathrm{d}z \, \mathrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{2} \left[ \int_{0}^{2-y} y^2 + yz + 2y \, \mathrm{d}z \right] \mathrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{2} \left[ (y^2+2y)z + \dfrac{1}{2}yz^2 \right]_{z=0}^{z=2-y} \mathrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{2} (y^2+2y)(2-y) + \dfrac{1}{2}y(2-y)^2 \, \mathrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{2} (4y - y^3) + \dfrac{1}{2}y(4-4y+y^2) \, \mathrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{2} -\dfrac{1}{2}y^3 - 2y^2 + 6y \, \mathrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \left[ -\dfrac{1}{8}y^4 - \dfrac{2}{3}y^3 + 3y^2 \right]_{y=0}^{y=2} \\[5pt] & = -2 - \dfrac{16}{3} + 12\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{14}{3} \end{align*}

example.title: Evaluating a Triple Integral Over a Type II Region

question.text:
Evaluate the triple integral $ \displaystyle \iiint\limits_R 12x \: \mathrm{d}V $ over the region $R,$ shown above.

Hint: All surfaces, except for the front one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.
question.explanation:
Notice that our solid can be written as the type II region

\[ R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (y,z) \in D, \:\: 0 \leq x \leq 1+y+z \big\}, \]

where

\[ D = \big\{ (y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 1 \big\} \]

is the projection of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane, shown below.

Hence, we can express the region $R$ as

\[ R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq x \leq 1+y+z \big\} \]

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

\[ \iiint \limits_{R} 12x \: \textrm{d}V = \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{1+y+z} 12x \: \mathrm{d}x \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}y. \]

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x$, treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:

\begin{align*} \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{1+y+z} 12x \: \mathrm{d}x \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}y &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{1} \left[ \int_{0}^{1+y+z} 12x \: \mathrm{d}x \right] \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{1} \big[ 6x^2 \big]_{x=0}^{x=1+y+z} \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{1} 6 (1+y+z)^2 \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{1} (6+6y^2+6z^2 +12yz+12y+12z) \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}y \end{align*}

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $y$ as a constant:

\begin{align*} \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{1} (6+6y^2+6z^2 +12yz+12y+12z) \: \mathrm{d}z \: \mathrm{d}y &= \int_{0}^{1} \left[ \int_{0}^{1} (6+6y^2+6z^2 +12yz+12y+12z) \: \mathrm{d}z \right] \mathrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \big[ 6z+6y^2z+2z^3 +6yz^2+12yz+6z^2 \big]_{z=0}^{z=1} \: \mathrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \left( 6+6y^2+2 +6y+12y+6 \right) \: \mathrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \left( 6y^2+18y+14 \right)\: \mathrm{d}y \end{align*}

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y{:}$

\begin{align*} \int_{0}^{1} \left( 6y^2+18y+14 \right) \: \mathrm{d}y &= \big[ 2y^3+9y^2+14y \big]_{y=0}^{y=1} \\[5pt] &= \left( 2 + 9 +14 \right) - 0 \\[5pt] &= 25. \end{align*}
